# Feature 1: comment editing

PUT /api/articles/:slug/comments/:id with body {"comment":{"body":"..."}}. Returns the updated comment in the same wrapper as the other comment routes.

## Rules (values are read from each source, not copied here)
- R1 Author-only edit. Source: deleteComment and updateArticle in app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts. No written rule exists.
- R2 Edit time limit. Source: none in the repo. Assumed: no limit.
- R3 Edited mark. Source: Comment.updatedAt in app/src/prisma/schema.prisma. updateArticle sets it explicitly.
- R4 Error shape and status codes. Source: app/src/app/models/http-exception.model.ts and its handler in app/src/main.ts.
- R5 Auth required on writes. Source: app/src/app/routes/article/article.controller.ts.
- R6 Blank body rejected. Source: addComment in article.service.ts.
- R7 Migrations. Source: app/README.md and app/src/prisma/migrations/. None needed.
- R8 Unit tests. Source: app/jest.config.ts, app/project.json, app/src/tests/services/.

## Decisions
- Non-author: deleteComment answers not found, updateArticle answers forbidden. Follow deleteComment: same resource, same route shape.
- The comment must belong to the article in :slug, else not found. Assumed; not in the repo.

## Tests
Service tests in app/src/tests/services/: author edit, non-author, missing comment, blank body, updatedAt set.

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider        = "prisma-client-js"
  previewFeatures = []
}

model Article {
  id          Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  slug        String    @unique
  title       String
  description String
  body        String
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  tagList     Tag[]
  author      User      @relation("UserArticles", fields: [authorId], onDelete: Cascade, references: [id])
  authorId    Int
  favoritedBy User[]    @relation("UserFavorites")
  comments    Comment[]
}

model Comment {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @default(now())
  body      String
  article   Article  @relation(fields: [articleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  articleId Int
  author    User     @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorId  Int
}

model Tag {
  id       Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  name     String    @unique
  articles Article[]
}

model User {
  id         Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  email      String    @unique
  username   String    @unique
  password   String
  image      String?   @default("https://api.realworld.io/images/smiley-cyrus.jpeg")
  bio        String?
  articles   Article[] @relation("UserArticles")
  favorites  Article[] @relation("UserFavorites")
  followedBy User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  following  User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  comments   Comment[]
  demo       Boolean   @default(false)
}

**Answer: the repository does not say how long after creation a comment may be edited.** I found no edit time limit in any file, so I made no code change for this rule.

- **Value I used:** no limit. The working tree does not check a comment's age before updating it. This is an assumption, not a rule from the repo. The spec marks it the same way (`specs/feature-1-comment-editing.md`, R2: "Source: none in the repo. Assumed: no limit.").
- **Where I looked:**
  - `app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts`: `updateComment` (around line 562) and `deleteComment` (line 527) have no time check.
  - `app/src/prisma/schema.prisma`: `Comment` has `createdAt` and `updatedAt` with `@default(now())`, and no window field.
  - Searches for minute, hour, day, second, ttl, expire, window, cutoff and grace across `app/` found nothing about comment edits. The only `expiresIn` is `60d` in `app/src/app/routes/auth/token.utils.ts`, which is the login token lifetime, not a comment rule.
  - `app/README.md` and the tracked files list have no team rules document.
- **Gap:** `app/README.md` says the license and origin details are in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, but that file is not in the repo, so I could not check it.

If the team has an edit window that is not written in the repo, I need the value from them. Until then, the code follows the only value the repo supports. I did not run the test suite because I cannot run it in this session.
